summary: Retested the iteration_8 fixes. Fixed and working: boosting a job through the real UI with Stripe (4242 card), an admin paying a boost for a contractor's job, origin allow-list, empty-body handling, unpaid-status regressions, and seed script password validation. NEW CRITICAL REGRESSION: the $19.99 plans (crew_monthly and contractor_basic) are never granted after a real Stripe payment, but the UI still shows 'Payment confirmed!'. Cause: emergentintegrations converts the price to cents with int(amount*100), so 19.99 becomes 1998. Stripe charges $19.98. The new strict _status_matches check compares 19.98 to the stored 19.99, logs 'amount/currency did not match', and does not fulfil. The transaction stays 'pending'.

critical.endpoint: GET /api/payments/stripe/status/{sid} (and every status/webhook path that uses _status_matches / _transaction_amount_matches)
critical.issue: Any price where int(p*100) truncates is never fulfilled: 19.99 becomes 1998 (crew_monthly, contractor_basic) and 79.99 becomes 7998 (the staging monthly_price setting). Reproduced: testcrew2 paid crew_monthly session cs_test_a1TMZ8R8... Stripe returned amount_total=1998 and the tx stayed payment_status=pending. The user stayed on crew_annual and backend.err.log shows 'Stripe checkout amount/currency did not match its local transaction (polling)'. Prices of 9.99, 39.99, 99, 2.99 and 15.99 work.

The response returns Stripe's payment_status='paid' even when the server refused to fulfil (amount mismatch), so the frontend tells the user it succeeded. The response should carry a 'fulfilled' or 'granted' flag, and the UI should check that flag instead of payment_status.

ui_bugs.issue: Two identical 'Payment received! Your job is boosted for 7 days.' toasts and two status calls. Under React.StrictMode the first poll is already in flight when cleanup sets stopped=true, and done() runs anyway because 'stopped' is only checked before the await. Fix: check stopped after the await, or use a ref guard like handledReturn.

integration_issues.issue: UI shows one 'Payment confirmed!' toast and navigates to /crew/dashboard, but the subscription is NOT updated (amount truncation bug above).

passed_checks: Boost via UI as contractor3 on job a0b7944a: the return URL is /contractor/dashboard?boost_session_id=cs_...&job_id=..., the page calls GET boost/stripe/status, shows the success toast and clears the query params. Job is_featured=true with boost_expires_at set; tx paid with job_owner_id set.

Admin-paid boost on job 267eeed3 with origin_url=https://evil.example.com: after paying, Stripe redirected to the preview domain (allow-list works). The status call as admin returned paid and featured the job. The tx has user_id=admin and job_owner_id=contractor3. The second status call returned already_processed.

Empty body (with no Content-Type, with application/json, and malformed JSON) on boost/stripe returns 200, boost/paypal returns 503, verified-contractor/create-session (fresh unverified contractor) returns 200, and contact-unlock returns 200 or 400. No 500s.
Evil origin_url accepted and replaced for stripe/create-session, verified-contractor and guest-job. paypal/create-order returns 503.
Unpaid verified-contractor, contact-unlock and guest-job sessions grant nothing. Emergency status returns 404 for an unknown session.

SubscriptionPage: card is selected by default, the label reads 'Crew Monthly plan', choosing PayPal shows paypal-unavailable, and switch-to-stripe-btn works. Exactly one confirmed toast and one status call.

seed_staging.py: STAGING_SUPERADMIN_PASSWORD=weak and STAGING_ADMIN_PASSWORD=password each exit 2 and no database is created. The happy path ends READY (exit 0). seed_staging_safety.sh: all PASS. All *_qa DBs dropped.

Unit tests: test_payment_security.py + test_staging_config.py gave 50 passed, 1 skipped. test_iteration8_payments_e2e.py: 18/18 passed. test_iteration9_payment_fixes.py: 16 passed, 1 skipped (crew already has contact access to contractor3; contact-unlock was covered by curl as contractor3 to testcrew2, which returned 200).
action_items: CRITICAL: Fix the cents mismatch. Either pass amounts so int(amount*100) is exact (for example compute cents with Decimal and pass cents/100 + 1e-9, or round(amount*100) yourself if the library allows it), or compare in _transaction_amount_matches against the cents the library actually charges (int(float(tx.amount)*100)). The fix must not loosen the check to a float tolerance. Add a unit test for 19.99 and 79.99.

Make the status endpoints return a 'fulfilled' boolean (true only after the grant succeeded or when already_processed is set). Have SubscriptionPage, the ContractorDashboard boost and verified flows, and the emergency flow show success only when it is true.
Optional: reconcile testcrew2's stuck pending tx cs_test_a1TMZ8R8... after the fix (they were charged $19.98 in test mode).
Low: dedupe the boost-return toast (StrictMode double-run).
critical_code_review_comments: payment_routes.py is 1219 lines; split it into subscription, boost, verified, unlock, guest and emergency modules.
The polling status endpoints echo the provider status instead of the local grant result, so the client can't tell a refused fulfilment from a success.
seed_data_creation: Real test-mode payments: contractor3 jobs a0b7944a and 267eeed3 are now featured. testcrew2 has a pending crew_monthly tx (cs_test_a1TMZ8R8...). The temporary test_iter9_* contractor was deleted by the fixture.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<preview> /root/.venv/bin/python -m pytest backend/tests/test_iteration9_payment_fixes.py backend/tests/test_iteration8_payments_e2e.py. To verify the cents fix, pay crew_monthly ($19.99) as testcrew2 at /subscription with 4242, then check that the DB tx is paid and subscription_plan is crew_monthly; don't trust the toast alone. contractor3's remaining non-featured open job is df476ad8 (Garage Demolition Cleanup), which you can use for the boost UI retest.
rca of the issue: emergentintegrations/payments/stripe/checkout.py:131 does amount_in_cents = int(request.amount * 100). 19.99*100 = 1998.9999999999998, which becomes 1998. Stripe charges and reports amount_total=1998. _status_matches/_transaction_amount_matches (added this iteration) compares Decimal 19.98 to 19.99 and returns False, so fulfil_subscription_tx is skipped. The endpoint still returns payment_status='paid', so the UI shows a success toast. To reproduce: run /tmp/q4.py (StripeCheckout.get_checkout_status on cs_test_a1TMZ8R8...), which shows amount_total=1998.
